Change page_mkwrite to allow implementations to return with the page
locked
column2: and also change it's callers (in page fault paths) to hold the

column1: lock until the page is marked dirty.  This allows the filesystem to have
full control of page dirtying events coming from the VM.
Rather than simply hold the page locked over the page_mkwrite call
call page_mkwrite with the page unlocked and allow callers to return with
it locked
column2: so filesystems can avoid LOR conditions with page lock.

column1: The problem with the current scheme is this: a filesystem that wants to
associate some metadata with a page as long as the page is dirty
perform this manipulation in its ->page_mkwrite.  It currently then must
return with the page unlocked and may not hold any other locks (according
to existing page_mkwrite convention).
In this window
column2: the VM could write out the page

column1: filesystem has no good way to detect that a dirty pte is about to be
attached
column2: so it will happily write out the page

column1: filesystem may manipulate the metadata to reflect that the page is no
longer dirty.
It is not always possible to perform the required metadata manipulation in
->set_page_dirty
column2: because that function cannot block or fail.  The

column1: filesystem may need to allocate some data structure
And the VM cannot mark the pte dirty before page_mkwrite
page_mkwrite is allowed to fail
column2: so we must not allow any window where the

column1: page could be written to if page_mkwrite does fail.
This solution of holding the page locked over the 3 critical operations
(page_mkwrite
column3: and finally setting the page dirty)

column1: closes out races nicely
column2: preventing page cleaning for writeout being

column1: initiated in that window.  This provides the filesystem with a strong
synchronisation against the VM here.
- Sage needs this race closed for ceph filesystem.
- Trond for NFS (http://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=12913).
- I need it for fsblock.
- I suspect other filesystems may need it too (eg. btrfs).
- I have converted buffer.c to the new locking. Even simple block allocation
under dirty pages might be susceptible to i_size changing under partial page
at the end of file (we also have a buffer.c-side problem here
be fixed properly without this patch).
- Other filesystems (eg. NFS
column2: maybe btrfs) will need to change their

column1: page_mkwrite functions themselves.
[ This also moves page_mkwrite another step closer to fault
eventually allow page_mkwrite to be moved into ->fault
filesystem calldown and page lock/unlock cycle in __do_fault. ]
